title: Best True-Crime & Real-Story Series
intro: The best true-crime and real-event series do not just reconstruct what happened - they interrogate why the systems around the crime allowed it, enabled it, or ignored it. This list covers the gold standard: meticulously sourced, morally serious, and lit by the kind of storytelling that turns documented history into essential television.

picks.title: Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story
picks.one_line: The definitive account of India's biggest securities fraud - Pratik Gandhi's performance is landmark television, and the financial architecture of the scam is explained with rare clarity.

picks.title: Making a Murderer
picks.one_line: The Netflix docuseries that broke the genre into the mainstream - Steven Avery's case opened a decade of debate about wrongful conviction and the machinery of rural American justice.

picks.title: The Jinx: The Life and Deaths of Robert Durst
picks.one_line: Andrew Jarecki's six-part HBO documentary ends with one of the most astonishing accidental confessions in non-fiction television history.

picks.title: Inventing Anna
picks.one_line: The Sorokin con reconstructed as a stylish Netflix drama - Julia Garner plays Anna with a ferocity that makes the audience complicit in rooting for her fraud.

picks.title: Bad Vegan
picks.one_line: A four-part Netflix docuseries about the downfall of a Manhattan raw-food restaurant empire - a study in how extraordinary charm weaponises reasonable people.

picks.title: Delhi Crime
picks.one_line: The 2012 Nirbhaya case, told from the Delhi Police investigation's perspective - International Emmy-winning Indian television that is difficult and necessary in equal measure.

picks.title: The Dropout
picks.one_line: Amanda Seyfried's Elizabeth Holmes is the year's most compulsive television performance - Theranos deconstructed as tragedy-comedy, with Silicon Valley's delusion rendered at clinical precision.

faq.q: Which true-crime series is the most important for Indian audiences specifically?
faq.a: Scam 1992 is required viewing for anyone who wants to understand Indian financial markets, the 1992 bull run, and how regulatory capture enables fraud at scale. Delhi Crime is the other essential Indian entry - a more painful but equally rigorous reconstruction.

The list mixes both formats deliberately. Making a Murderer, The Jinx, and Bad Vegan are pure documentary. Scam 1992, Inventing Anna, The Dropout, and Delhi Crime are dramatisations based on documented record. Each title's page notes the format, and all are rigorously sourced from public reporting.
